topic: Using std::reverse with Iterators in Modern C++
explanation: In C++, algorithms from the Standard Template Library (STL) operate on iterator ranges, allowing flexible and efficient manipulation of container elements. The 'std::reverse' algorithm reverses the order of elements within a specified range, defined by two iterators. Modern C++ emphasizes the use of iterators, auto type deduction, and range-based algorithms to write concise, safe, and expressive code. Proper understanding of iterator validity and range boundaries is crucial to avoid runtime errors such as iterator invalidation or range violations.
